newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FALL IN LIQUID, QUIET MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FALL IN LIQUID, QUIET MARKET.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted softer on Friday in a quiet and very liquid market.

"In these circumstances we don't foresee any changes in the rates," one money market dealer said, adding that the central Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) was indicating a surplus of around Z$2 billion.
He said discount houses were buying Bankers Acceptance bills at 18.20 percent and selling them at 17.50 percent, down from 18.60 percent and 17.80 percent respectively.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted at 19 percent (buying) against 19.50 percent on Christmas Eve and at 17.75 percent (selling) from 19 percent.
Call money was rated at 17.50 percent on Friday from 18 percent before the Christmas holidays.
